factor_diagnostics.value_notes: NOAA describes Pacific cod as near-bottom fish on mud, sand and clay, moving from deep outer/upper shelf spawning grounds (about 300 to over 800 feet) in winter to shallower shelf feeding grounds in summer. A 2022 Bering Sea survey recorded bottom depths of 18-183 m in northern and eastern shelf areas; other NOAA species records span a much broader range. The configured 20-200 m interval is a reasonable shelf screen but not a universal depth preference across regions and seasons.
